cur:monumental-san-led-to-calvary.summary: The bearded Christ, haloed and robed in purple, is led forward by a soldier in a blue tunic, while Simon of Cyrene, in red, carries the long cross beside him. In keeping with Early Christian reticence, the cycle passes from this scene directly to the empty tomb, without showing the Crucifixion itself.
facts: On the south wall the thirteen Passion and Resurrection scenes show Christ bearded; the cycle omits both the Flagellation and the Crucifixion.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.

walters:W.185.58V.summary: Christ stands bound to a slender pink column, naked except for a loincloth, his body marked with wounds. Two tormentors in brightly coloured tunics and hose lunge at him from either side with raised scourges, their twisting poses contrasting with his stillness. The black-and-white chequered floor and patterned gold ground give the small scene a jewel-like intensity.
facts: The book is named after Franchoise de Doffinnes, who owned it in the late 16th century; her family's later history is recorded on its final folios.

Its calendar follows the Use of Utrecht and its Hours of the Virgin largely the Use of the Windesheim Congregation, pointing to a Dutch origin; it contains both Latin and Dutch texts and twelve full-page miniatures by the Master of Walters 185.
walters:W.185.58V.notes: Museum date (1400–1425) applies to the whole Book of Hours; the date in our data (8th century) was an import error.
